mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 7% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer demand and corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE > 7.0 for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and pressures profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when RSAFS declines for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 1% signals improving manufacturing activity and economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when INDPRO rises > 1% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the civilian labor force participation rate (implied from UNRATE and PAYEMS) below 63% for two consecutive months signals structural labor shortages, which constrain economic growth and corporate earnings, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE + PAYEMS imply LFPR < 63% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of implied LFPR < 63% for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above 8% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related economic activity and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when HOUST rises > 8% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 98% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and economic growth, which reduces corporate earnings and supports negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when INDPRO < 98% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).
